headline: A survey by security firm Semperis finds that 84 percent of ransomware victims said attackers used AI in the attack.
score_reason: Kept at pool score 6: new vendor survey with striking figures, but self-reported and from a firm that sells security products.
importance_line: Companies and public bodies facing ransomware are told AI is now routine in attacks and that their own AI agents can be targeted, though the figures come from a vendor survey of 1,200 professionals.
summary: CBS News reports on the 2026 Ransomware Risk Report from cybersecurity firm Semperis, which surveyed 1,200 IT and security professionals in nine countries: 84 percent of ransomware victims said attackers used AI, 44 percent said attackers exploited their own AI systems, and 59 percent paid a ransom at least once. Chris Inglis, a former White House National Cyber Director and Semperis board member, says autonomous ransomware attacks are already happening, but argues the weakness that lets attackers in is usually the same as before AI and that defenders should use AI too.
notes: Survey figures are respondents' own reports; Inglis is a Semperis board member.
